structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E016.
1. Where the accuracy came from: averaging (E005, about +1.0 pp), Muon (E006, +0.66 pp), and pixels or capacity in the final phase. E011 is the strongest evidence for the last one: cutting the 32 px share and the low-resolution floor cost 1.4 pp. Narrowing to 512 in E010 cost about 0.4 pp, and the tip pays that back by running 9.5 epochs. The scalar knobs (LS in E013, Muon lr in E014, LR→0 in E009) all landed within ±0.3 pp.
2. My E016 miss. Halving WD gave +0.33 pp, from 0.7574 to 0.7607. I had called WD inert because Muon applies none and the filters are renormalized. But WD still acts on the head and the BN biases, which are coupled through SGD. A mechanism nobody has named: the head WD works as a logit-temperature knob. The output is scaled by 1/9 and LS is 0.3, so the head norm sets how confident the logits can get. Halving WD lets the head norm grow, which effectively sharpens the logits for 100 classes. That could be a real effect of about 0.2 pp, plus reshuffle noise. If so, the head WD alone (or zero head WD) is a small lever that nobody has isolated. I'd still discount the tip to a true mean of about 0.758.
3. Noise. A re-run of the same binary is bit-identical (E012). Any kernel or graph change reshuffles the per-seed results by about ±0.3 pp on the 3-seed mean (E015 gained 0.27 pp with "identical math"). The loop picks lucky reshuffles when it keeps results, so the 40-seed mean is probably 0.1-0.3 pp below the 3-seed tip. Time noise is about ±1%.
4. Lookahead on Muon's fixed-norm sphere. The pull shrinks the filter norms, Muon renormalizes them, and the net effect is angular damping plus a reset to a consensus point. A write-only EMA loses this, and its averaged BN buffers are mismatched with the averaged weights. I expect I022 to lose accuracy.
5. Time is GPU FLOPs. CUDA graphs gained under 1%. Per-step pixel cost is 24 px : 28 px : 32 px = 0.56 : 0.77 : 1. Per-image conv FLOPs split roughly 18% / 49% / 33% across group 1 / group 2 / group 3, so group 2 is the biggest block. Cutting group 2 to 320 removes about 16% of FLOPs, or about 9% of time. Cutting low-resolution steps is cheap in accuracy only while the 32 px tail is untouched.
6. Note that the tip runs 9.5 epochs, not 9, so the 40/30/30 fractions are taken over 9.5 epochs.
What I'm unsure of: the held-out mean of the tip; whether max-autotune reselects the same kernels from a cold cache; whether the head-WD effect is real.

forecasts.reason: A write-only EMA loses the reset-on-sphere damping, and its averaged BN buffers are mismatched, so it should land below the tip by more than 0.3 pp.
About 8% fewer pixel-FLOPs with the 32 px tail intact; the loss should be small (about 0.4 pp), unlike E011, which shrank the tail.
The cut epochs are cheap 24 px steps, so the loss should be well below the 0.3 pp per 0.5 epoch slope; it says little about the smooth epoch dial.
Re-runs are bit-identical (as in E012) unless a cold-cache autotune picks different kernels; I expect the held-out mean to be about 0.2 pp below the seeds 0-2 mean.
The Muon scalar knobs have been flat so far; the change will mostly reshuffle seeds.
About 16% fewer conv FLOPs saves about 9% of time but costs capacity, roughly 0.5 pp, which is about the cost of E010's narrowing.

cruxes: Is E016's +0.33 pp a real head-WD (logit-temperature) effect or a reshuffle? Test: set head WD to 0 or halve it again, with the BN-bias WD fixed.
Is accuracy set mainly in the 32 px tail? If so, removing low-resolution steps (I023/I024) is nearly free, and the biggest time cut comes from trimming early epochs and group-2 width, not the tail.
What is the tip's held-out 10-seed mean? This sets how much of the 0.76 margin can be spent on time cuts.
